preamble: [d] becomes [s] in Indo-European through cluster effects, not as an unconditioned change. Before a dental, PIE *-dt- (and *-tt-) gives Greek and Iranian -st-, and Italic and Germanic -ss-. Before *s, d assimilates totally (Latin ad- + s- > ass-, Homeric Greek ποσσί).

examples.note: 'seen', participle of videō; via Proto-Italic *wissos, with -ss- simplified after the long vowel.
'sit by, attend'; prefix /d/ totally assimilated to the following /s/.
dative plural of πούς 'foot'; stem-final δ assimilated to σ.
'certain, known', past participle of *witaną 'to know'; continued in Old English and Old Saxon wiss and Old Norse viss.
